scopeNote: No fee/recipe research this wave. No new Driver, no CAC, no desktop shell. Zero model and native turns. wave03-b-native cap4 remainder stays UNKNOWN and unspendable; E's pilot grant untouched; all eight user instances preserved.

B1.label: the four public modules compile under main strict typing
B1.method: real public types for request/result/refusal shapes; strict was not relaxed, no `any` escape was introduced, no useful export was removed

interfaceDefectsClosed.fix: the admitted input is snapshotted synchronously before any await, so mutating the caller object during the reservation cannot change what the transport receives
the token binds the admitted startTurn IMPLEMENTATION as well as the transport object, and calls it with the transport as receiver, so a later method swap has no effect
review-sender.ts exports a module-level send; it refuses unless the request names a review-sender/1 b-sender entry, and even then refuses for want of an owned transport and a measured bound

B1.defaultPathUntouched: the personal chain keeps its existing authenticated proof; the new index exports do not wire any untested sender into the default path

B2.label: diagnostics and current resources read through the single authenticated proof
B2.singleProof: verifiedRunnerInspection() / the one WeakMap in recovery-transport.ts; no parallel registry was created
B2.observationOnly: a description never grants release: releaseBarrierSatisfied requires an authenticated proof and complete coverage
B2.positiveAndNegative: authenticated socket positive control plus refusal of plain JSON, JSON round-trip and hand-assembled lookalikes

B3.label: bounded closure of the experimental sender interface
B3.frozenInput: snapshotted before the reservation await; the same reference is what the transport receives
B3.fixedImplementation: startTurn is captured at issuance and invoked with the transport as receiver
B3.oneUse: claimed synchronously before the await; a refusal, throw or unknown outcome consumes the token and is never refunded
B3.reservationId: supplied by the caller's hook and echoed back by the module-level entry; the same owner keeps it
B3.noCliSender: no second CLI sender exists; the module-level entry is inert without an owned transport and a measured bound
B3.defaultZeroSends: with no bound the default path sends nothing and refreshes nothing
B3.boundary: this proves the refusal chain and a fixture single send. It does NOT claim to defend against a caller who already holds arbitrary host code, and it does not prove real review or native behaviour.

B4.label: persistent control and restart matrix
matrix: answers keep attempt and epoch identity
different steers get distinct command identities
a reconnect adds no duplicate begin
an old-attempt proof does not release a new attempt
an unproven stop never decays to stopped
notTested: real vendor stop/answer/steer/disconnect/reconnect and unknown-send reconciliation
the process-wide epoch high-water mark across a real restart, which needs durable storage owned by core/storage

B5.label: recovery and diagnostics consumption for main/D
B5.activeOrUnknownResourcesBlock: an active or indeterminate writer keeps the barrier closed and new execution refuses
B5.newStateDoesNotForget: creating a new state or generation releases nothing; no observation never satisfies the barrier
B5.ownershipBoundary: the resource set is authoritative for the endpoint it was authenticated against, and an observation is never permission to clean up another instance
B5.actionableReasons: refusals carry an explanation and the invalid inference they refused to make, rather than collapsing to an empty PASS or an empty set

layers.native: NOT_TESTED - no vendor turn was executed

limitations: all sender transports and reservations are local in-memory fakes; no ledger is read or written
the sender cannot prove the caller's process identity; grant authority is the ledger audit
the module-level send entry is inert by design; it is not a working native sender today
B resource facts do not replace main's current-binding and exact registered-manifest validation
no current personal-product permission bypass is claimed; the findings concern an experimental helper interface

nextConsumerSteps.main: the four modules now compile under your strict settings; call describeResourceFacts only with an authenticated proof, and use describeRuntime for read-only facts
nextConsumerSteps.D: describeRuntime yields exact executable/profile facts with paths redacted by default and no credential access
nextConsumerSteps.E: consume the module-level send through the review-sender/1 b-sender entry; it is currently inert, which is the supported answer given the blocked recipe
